data.name: Malti
data.gender_notes: Malti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'mālatī', meaning 'nectar of immortality' or 'giving life'. In Hindu mythology, Malti is the name of a woman who was transformed into a tree and provided the nectar of immortality to Shiva. The name Malti carries the meaning “Nectar of immortality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Malti usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of immortality and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the transformative power of love and devotion.
data.etymology: Malti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of immortality.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Malti total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Malti carries a rich cultural heritage in Hindu mythology. It symbolizes the bestowal of nectar, signifying prosperity, longevity, and abundance in one‘s life. The name is also associated with the showering of blessings and nurturing qualities, which are highly esteemed qualities in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Malti reflects the spiritual concept of offering and receiving nourishment. It encourages the recipient to become a giver and embody the qualities of compassion and selflessness. The name also symbolizes transformation, as seen in the mythological tale of Malti being transformed into a tree. This story conveys the idea of transcending one's physical form and offering spiritual sustenance to others, ultimately leading to spiritual growth and enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Malti is a popular Sanskrit name for girls, derived from the word 'Malati' meaning 'garland of flowers'. It is a beautiful name with deep cultural significance in India, symbolizing the beauty and grace of nature.

historical_references.reference: Malti, also known as Malati, was a renowned poetess and a lover of King Kalidasa. It is said that she was a fairy, who was enchanted by the great poet's brilliance and fell in love with him. They wrote poetry together under the name 'Meghe Dhoka' meaning 'Cloud Messenger'. This literature is considered a masterpiece of Indian literature and is included in the Sahitya Akademi list of 100 best books in Indian literature.

Malti, also known as Mallika, was a queen of the Sangam period in Tamil Nadu, South India. She is remembered in Tamil literature for her poetic works, which were deeply emotional and dealt with themes of love, longing and separation. Her work is considered an important contribution to the Tamil Sangam literature.
